description: Stable identifiers for every party and independent label in the election data. The id is curated and independent of the display name, so two organisations with the same name are distinguishable and one organisation with several name spellings is not split.
idPolicy: Ids are permanent. Renaming an organisation changes `name`, never `id`. Where two entities would otherwise collide, the id carries a disambiguator (green-ni / green-ie, pup / progressive-unionist-1938).

types.independent-label: a ballot description, not an organisation
types.banner: an agreed non-party label (Unity, Anti H-Block)

aliasResolution: An alias is a string, optionally narrowed by `bodies` and by a half-open date window [from, until). The first entity whose alias matches string + body + date wins; a string may be shared by several entities when their scopes are disjoint.
provisional: true means auto-generated from a single observed string and not reviewed: the id is a slug of the name, there is no source, and no lifespan. Curating one means confirming the alias set, setting a type, and adding dates and a source.

entities.name: United Kingdom Unionist Party
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: 'UK Unionist Party' is the same organisation under a second string, used only by the local-government dataset (22 candidacies, 1997-2005). Robert McCartney's 1995-06-15 North Down by-election candidacy carries the string 'UKUP' ten months before this founding date and is reported as a contradiction; the party was constituted after that by-election, so the label appears to have been applied retrospectively. Last candidacy is 2007-03-07, eighteen months before dissolution. The Northern Ireland Unionist Party split from the UKUP in 1999 and is recorded separately as niup, with splitFrom pointing here; note the two organisations wound up within six months of each other in 2008 (NIUP 10 March, UKUP 4 September).

entities.name: Northern Ireland Unionist Party
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: A SPLIT from the UKUP, not a succession: the UKUP continued and contested until 2007, so predecessor/successor would wrongly assert that it ended in 1999. Two strings, both this organisation: 'NI Unionist Party' (4 candidacies, 2001 Westminster and 2003 Assembly) and 'Northern Ireland Unionist Party' (8, 2001 local government). All 12 fall inside the window. The party's last candidacy is 2003-11-26, more than four years before dissolution — a gap that is invisible to the derived lastYear, which would have reported 2003 as the end.

entities.name: People Before Profit
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: Deliberately NOT scoped by body, unlike the Green entry. The 'PBP' string covers 75 candidacies on NI bodies and 33 in dail-eireann and ireland-european, and People Before Profit organises across both jurisdictions as one party, so both are attributed here. If that is wrong and the two should be separate organisations, this entry needs splitting the way Green (NI) is. 'Solidarity-PBP' (86 candidacies, 2019-2024, dail-eireann and ireland-european only) is NOT included: it is the joint ticket registered with Solidarity, and a joint ticket is its own registration rather than the component party — the same treatment given to UCUNF.

entities.name: Vanguard Unionist Progressive Party
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: The supplied founding date is that of Ulster Vanguard, the movement, whereas the party string in the data is specifically the Vanguard Unionist Progressive Party, which was constituted in 1973. Recorded as supplied; if the party rather than the movement is meant, this needs the 1973 date. The distinction changes nothing in the results, since the first candidacy is 1973-05-30 either way. Three 1982 candidacies fall four and a half years after dissolution and are reported as contradictions: William Craig (Belfast East), John Dunlop and Robert Overend (Mid Ulster), in the 1982 Assembly election. Craig founded the party, so this is the label outliving the organisation rather than a mis-attribution.

entities.name: Vanguard Unionist Progressive Party
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: Deliberately carries the SAME `name` as entity vanguard and a different id — the case the id scheme exists for. Shares the party string with its predecessor; the two are separated by their lifespans alone, which are disjoint (1972-02-09..1978-02-20 and 1982-08-30..1987-05-27), so no alias scoping is needed. This claims all three Vanguard candidacies at the 1982-10-20 Assembly election: William Craig (Belfast East), John Dunlop and Robert Overend (both Mid Ulster). Craig's is the only one of the three that is his own; the other two are captured because they carry the same label inside the same window. Narrow the alias to Craig alone if that is not intended. Not a succession — there is a four-and-a-half-year gap after the original dissolved — hence revivalOf rather than predecessor/successor.

entities.name: Ecology Party (Northern Ireland)
entities.source: PROVISIONAL — supplied by repository owner 2026-07-26 as a working value pending confirmation
entities.notes: The founding date is the date of the 1981 local elections, which is when the Ecology label first appears in the data (Malcolm Samuel, Coleraine Area B; Avril McCandless, Coleraine Area C). It is a placeholder for the party's actual founding, not a sourced date, and should be replaced. The dissolution date is the founding of the Green Party, i.e. a same-day handover.

entities.name: Green Party (Northern Ireland)
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26
entities.notes: The 'Green' string is scoped to NI bodies. The same string carries 264 candidacies in dail-eireann and ireland-european which belong to the Green Party in the Republic, a separate organisation with no dates supplied here; those are deliberately left unattributed rather than folded in. 'Green / Ecology' is a label used only by the local-government dataset, across 1981-2011, and is therefore shared with the predecessor and resolved by date.

entities.name: Progressive Unionist Party
entities.source: supplied by repository owner, 2026-07-26 (year only)
entities.notes: Only the year is known, so the date is recorded as 1977-01-01 with foundedPrecision 'year'. That 01-01 is padding, NOT a claim about the day — the first entry in the registry to use this, and the reason the field exists. Status is 'unknown' rather than 'active': no dissolution date was supplied and none is inferred, though the party's most recent candidacy is 2023. Claims only the string 'PUP'; the ten 1938 Stormont candidacies labelled 'Progressive Unionist' are a different organisation, entity progressive-unionist-1938. One 1973 candidacy (Elizabeth Roulton, Ballymena Area C, 107 votes) falls four years before this founding and is reported as a contradiction.
